title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1967-10-22

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1967 show highlighted by a blistering "The Other One"/Cryptical sequence and soaring Jerry Garcia solos.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean sound‑board source that sounds great for its era, with all instruments clear and well balanced. The performance is tight and electric – the band rolls through powerful versions of "Lovelight", "Beat It", "New Potato Caboose" and especially the debut Cryptical → Other One suite, where Jerry’s lead work is described as volcanic. Vocals and harmonies are on point, making this a repeat‑listenable gem from the early psychedelic period.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (mostly 4–5) and enthusiastic comments about both musical performance and sound quality push the overall score into the excellent range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers note a crisp, clear mix with all instruments audible; some mention "pretty good for its age" but no major flaws are reported.

standout_songs: The Other One (Cryptical → Other One suite)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows tightly with high energy; the Cryptical > Too > Cryptical (Other One) sequence is singled out as a highlight, and the band stays together without sloppiness throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is described as volcanic, brutal yet sweet, delivering one of the greatest lead solos of 1967 on "The Other One".
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh provides strong counter‑point to Jerry and is praised for his bass work during the New Potato/Cryptical sections.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s vocals on "Beat It" are noted as especially good, a rarity in this early period.
band_member_comments.Drums: Only Bill Kreutzmann is present on drums (one‑drummer show), delivering solid, tight rhythm; a few reviewers mistakenly reference Mickey Hart but the consensus notes the single‑drummer setup.
